# Stationarity and chord identities for an interior three-triangle extremal model

The sharp three-planar-fiber existence conclusion is already covered by accepted fact 2a8c2bc6d7992c5e (and the all-count planar result 5a8e9f2c38a69fb0). It is not submitted as a new theorem here. The retained mathematical content is the stationarity, source-weight, and weighted chord argument in the following restricted model.

Let positive-area triangles K_0,K_1,K_2 satisfy (K_0+K_2)/2 subset int(K_1), and place them at integer bases 0,1,2. Let beta denote their maximum normalized ambient halfspace depth. Assume the triple is a local minimum among nearby compatible positive-area triangle triples. The calculations below concern this local model, including nonsmooth cap coincidences.

## 1. Which fibers can be deepest

Write a=area(K_0), b=area(K_1), c=area(K_2), M=a+b+c, and gamma=4/9.
An endpoint fiber can be isolated by a sufficiently large integer tilt of
any continuous halfspace. Its restricted maximum depth is therefore EXACTLY

    gamma a/M at index0,       gamma c/M at index2.

The lower bound is its own triangle centroid's ordinary Grünbaum bound;
for the upper bound use the sharp triangle bound and isolate that fiber.
The middle restricted maximum is at least gamma b/M from its own centroid.

At a local minimum the middle fiber must be globally deepest. Otherwise
slightly enlarge it about an interior point. Strict midpoint containment
persists. The endpoint maxima strictly decrease through the larger total
mass, while the middle remains below the former maximum by continuity and
its strict gap. This is a strict depth decrease, a contradiction.

Both endpoints cannot be deepest. That would imply a=c. The strict
containment and Brunn--Minkowski give

    b>area((K_0+K_2)/2)>=(sqrt(a)+sqrt(c))^2/4=a.

The middle's own-fiber guarantee would then exceed the endpoint maximum.
Consequently the middle is deepest and at most one endpoint is deepest.

## 2. Exact critical circuit covers and normalized stress

The middle restricted maximum is positive and is attained by the compact
cap-capacity lemma in candidate b989614dc4f86228, Section E.
It lies in the interior: at a boundary point with support normal u, strict
containment gives h_K0(u)+h_K2(u)<2h_K1(u). An integer tilt v strictly between
h_K0(u)-h_K1(u) and h_K1(u)-h_K2(u) makes the through-point cap meet only the
zero-area supporting face of K1. Thus every boundary point has depth zero.

At an interior restricted maximizer in the middle fiber, choose a minimal
positive circuit of active continuous cap normals. It has k=2 or3 caps,
all of mass beta M, through one common middle point c_*. Write its normals
and positive weights as

    H_j={v_j z+u_j.x>=b_j},
    sum_j rho_j u_j=0, rho_j>0, sum_j rho_j=1.

At each endpoint choose its three canonical triangle vertex-direction caps
through its centroid and give them a sufficiently large integer tilt to
exclude the other two fibers STRICTLY. Each such endpoint cap has mass
exactly gamma times that endpoint's area. Each of these three groups covers
its ENTIRE own continuous fiber because its weighted margins sum to zero
there. Caps at a nondeep endpoint have strict budget slack relative to beta M.

The strict midpoint containment makes arbitrary sufficiently small affine
variations of the THREE triangles independently admissible. Parameterize
these by x -> (I+A_z)x+c_z. Also vary each cap's integer normal v_j and
threshold b_j, keeping u_j and rho_j fixed, and impose the one linear
whole-fiber coverage inequality for its group anchored at z:

    C_z=sum_j rho_j(v_j z-b_j)>=0.

These inequalities ensure that all three groups continue to cover the
entire union at every nearby body. The given triple is consequently a local
maximizer of M under these coverage inequalities and cap budgets beta M_0,
where M_0 is its original mass: a larger feasible mass would give actual
maximum depth at most beta M_0/M<beta.

The normalized first-order separation from candidate 5e600a897e2488c6
applies here without any support-compatibility multipliers. To recall its
justification, the objective area derivative is linear in the independent
affine parameters. Each active cap has a compact convex set of generalized
first-order gradients, with the same boundary trace theta in its shape and
cap-motion terms. Common inner parallel erosion of each triangle is an
admissible affine variation: homothety about its incenter with factor
1-t/r, where r is its inradius, moves every facet inward by t. This erosion
has strictly negative pairing with EVERY
active cap-gradient choice. The positive patch of body boundary lying in
the open cap gives the strict loss. This yields a closed cap-gradient cone
plus the polar of the linear coverage tangent cone. Separation, followed by
a small erosion to strictify cap budgets, rules out failure of the normalized
objective representation. Thus there are nonnegative cap multipliers lambda
and coverage multipliers eta. Slack endpoint caps have lambda=0.

At coincident facets, theta may be measurable in the facet point if needed.
Its shape coefficient is nonnegative and at most one; this is the only
property of these nonsmooth traces needed below. All proper-section shape
formulas are ordinary derivatives.

Jointly dilate all continuous fibers and all cap pairs (v_j,b_j), leaving
u_j fixed. Every cap mass and M scale by the square of the dilation factor,
while each active homogeneous coverage inequality remains zero. Every
permitted generalized gradient has this same homothety derivative. Pairing
the normalized stress with that direction gives the exact identity

    sum_all_caps lambda_j=1/beta.                                 (1)

Only the middle group and at most one endpoint group carry multipliers.

## 3. Central affine stationarity

Translate continuous coordinates so the middle group's common anchor c_*
is zero. Every middle cap then cuts its triangle properly, with line
u_j.x=0. Let C_j be the area of its middle-triangle cap, S_j its section
length (for unit u_j), and X_j the section's first moment about the anchor.

The endpoint isolating caps exclude the middle fiber strictly, so they have
zero derivative under its independent affine variations. An affine middle
variation x -> (I+A)x+c gives cap derivative

    tr(A) C_j + u_j.A X_j + S_j u_j.c.

The objective derivative is tr(A)b. Therefore central translation and linear
stationarity give

    sum_j lambda_j S_j u_j=0,
    b tr(A)=sum_j lambda_j[tr(A) C_j+u_j.A X_j] for every A.

Since every section lies on u_j.x=0, choosing A=I shows

    sum_j lambda_j C_j=b.                                        (2)

Subtracting this trace part yields

    sum_j lambda_j X_j u_j^T=0.                                  (3)

All middle multipliers are positive. Otherwise the first equation would
supply a nonzero positive dependence on a proper subset of a minimal
positive circuit; all zero is ruled out by (2).

For k=2 the normals are opposite, the section is the same chord, and the
translation equation makes the two multipliers equal. The two caps partition
K_1 up to a null line, so their normalized weighted mean area fraction is
1/2.

For k=3 put a_j=lambda_j S_j>0 and m_j=X_j/S_j, the chord midpoint. The
continuous normals have rank2 and their relation space is one-dimensional.
For each coordinate, equation (3) says the coefficient vector
(a_j m_j,coordinate)_j is another relation among the u_j. It is therefore a
scalar multiple of (a_j). Hence all m_j coincide. Since they lie on all
three concurrent cap lines, their common midpoint is the anchor itself.
The following lemma now applies.

## 4. The weighted bisected-chord triangle lemma

Let a point of a triangle have positive barycentric coordinates
l_1,l_2,l_3. Suppose three distinct chord lines through it are each bisected
there, and their oriented cap normals form a positive circuit. Let positive
normalized weights theta_j satisfy the section-weighted balance
sum theta_j S_j u_j=0. Then the theta-weighted cap area fraction is at least
4/9.

Proof. A chord joining edges i and j and bisected at the point has endpoints
with barycentric coordinates

    (coordinate i=0, coordinate j=2 l_j, coordinate k=1-2 l_j),
    (coordinate i=2 l_i, coordinate j=0, coordinate k=1-2 l_i).

These are valid exactly when l_i,l_j<=1/2. If some l_i>1/2 there is only one
bisected chord line. If l_i=1/2, two of the three descriptions coincide, so
there are at most two distinct lines. A rank2 minimal three-normal circuit
therefore requires l_i<1/2 for all i. Its three lines are exactly the three
listed ones.

For the cap on the vertex-k side of the chord joining edges i,j, use the
unnormalized margin

    2-xi_i/l_i-xi_j/l_j,

where xi denotes barycentric coordinates. Its cap area fraction is
4 l_i l_j, and its coarea section mass is 4 area(T) l_i l_j. Positive
rescaling of a cap normal changes section length to the corresponding
coarea mass in its balance equation and does not alter the cap or weights.
The positive relation of these three margin normals has coefficients
rho_k=1-2 l_k, whose sum is1. Therefore the normalized section-balanced
weights are

    theta_k=l_k(1-2 l_k)/(1-2 sum_i l_i^2).

The weighted vertex-side fraction is exactly

    F=4 l_1 l_2 l_3/(1-2 sum_i l_i^2).                             (4)

It lies between4/9 and1/2. The lower bound is Schur's degree-three inequality
9 l_1 l_2 l_3 >= 1-2 sum l_i^2. For completeness, with x>=y>=z>=0,

    sum_cyclic x(x-y)(x-z)
      =(x-y)^2(x+y-z)+z(x-z)(y-z)>=0,

which, after using x+y+z=1, is precisely the required inequality. The upper
bound in (4) follows from

    (1-2 l_1)(1-2 l_2)(1-2 l_3)
       =1-2 sum_i l_i^2-8 l_1 l_2 l_3>=0.

For three unoriented rank2 normals, the positive-circuit orientation is
unique up to reversing all three: their relation space has dimension one.
Thus the only other case takes all three complementary caps, with the same
section-balanced weights and weighted fraction 1-F>=1/2. This proves the
lemma, including every possible cap orientation.

Apply the lemma with theta_j=lambda_j/L, L=sum_middle lambda_j. Equation (2)
gives weighted cap fraction 1/L. Hence

    sum_middle lambda_j<=1/gamma=9/4.                             (5)

The k=2 case gives the stronger bound2 and also satisfies (5).

## 5. The possible deepest endpoint group

If an endpoint is deepest, independently dilate its triangle about its
interior centroid. Its area derivative is twice its area, and each of its
canonical own caps has derivative twice gamma times its area.

Every middle-group cap generalized shape derivative under this expansion
is NONNEGATIVE. On ordinary facets its coefficient is the area inside the
open cap; on coincident facets it is a nonnegative trace theta. Every body
facet's outward homothety velocity about an interior point is strictly
positive. Holding cap parameters fixed adds no section-motion term.
Consequently its contribution to normalized stationarity is nonnegative,
including all boundary coincidences.

If e is that endpoint's area, stationarity thus gives

    2e >= (sum_endpoint lambda_j) 2 gamma e,

and therefore

    sum_endpoint lambda_j<=1/gamma.                              (6)

If no endpoint is deepest, every endpoint multiplier is zero. Combining
(1), (5), and (6) proves 1/beta<=2/gamma, or beta>=2/9.

## Scope

The strict midpoint containment is essential to this local theorem because
it permits independent affine variations of the three triangles. The result
forces any bad triangle-fiber extremizer onto active compatibility; it does
not analyze that boundary and does not imply the full OC statement. The
proof itself does not require smooth cap positions, an isolated median,
finite active-halfspace families, or favorable integer tilts at the middle.
